title: Proper Poincare duality
statement:
In the Poincare duality conventions [def-pod-conventions] of this chapter (the fixed setting), assume in addition that $X_0$ is proper, let $\Lambda \in \{ A,\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }\}$ with $A=A_{E,n}$, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda )$ be perfect over $\Lambda _X$ [def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x], let $K^\vee$ be the coefficient dual [def-pod-coefficient-dual-on-x] with Tate twist [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] $K^\vee (d)$, and let $\beta _K$ be the derived Poincare pairing [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing] (mixed-support cup product, evaluation, normalized smooth trace). Since $X$ is proper, the canonical comparison $R\Gamma _c(X,K)\cong R\Gamma (X,K)$ of proper compact-support comparison (the proper case of $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$, $f=a_X$) identifies $\beta _K$ with a perfect pairing [def-pod-perfect-derived-pairing]

$$
R\Gamma (X,K)\otimes _\Lambda^LR\Gamma \bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)[2d] \longrightarrow \Lambda,
$$

whose adjoint has inverse the canonical isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma (X,K)^\vee \xrightarrow {\  \sim \  } R\Gamma \bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)[2d].
$$

Over a field this gives perfect degreewise pairings

$$
H^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}\bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)\longrightarrow \Lambda ,
$$

and the line-valued form

$$
H^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\longrightarrow \Lambda (-d).
$$

Here the dual of a point complex means $C^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(C,\Lambda)$ at the selected coefficient stage, and ordinary and compact-support cohomology use [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Properness is in the sense of [def-weil-proper-morphism].

proof.text: Properness of the geometric fiber. In [def-pod-conventions], $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the base change of the structure morphism of $X_0$. The additional hypothesis that $X_0$ is proper means that this structure morphism is proper. Apply clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] to $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$. It follows that $a_X$ is proper. No properness of a different morphism is used.

source.place: Step 1, properness under base change; Stacks Tag 01W4

proof.text: The canonical comparison at the selected coefficient stage. For the proper structure morphism $a_X$, [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence] supplies the canonical finite-level comparison $Ra_{X!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{X*}$ associated with the identity compactification. Use [prop-weil-proper-compact-coincidence] for the same proper scheme $X$ and the coefficient conventions of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]; its statement is not restricted to finite coefficients. Thus it supplies $Ra_{X!}\cong Ra_{X*}$ also at $\mathcal O_E$, $E$ and the common $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ stage. Applying the point-fiber functor in that cohomology definition gives an isomorphism $e:C\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$, where $C=R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ and $Q=R\Gamma(X,K)$. Applying $H^i$ gives $e_i:H_c^i(X,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(X,K)$ for every integer $i$. These are the canonical comparisons, not arbitrary isomorphisms between complexes of equal dimensions.

source.place: Step 1, canonical global-section comparison; proper coincidence at all coefficient stages

proof.text: Read the specified pairing through the comparison. Put $D=R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]$. The definition [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing] gives the actual morphism $\beta_K:C\otimes^L_\Lambda D\to\Lambda$, namely mixed-support cup product followed by evaluation and normalized smooth trace. Define the pairing on ordinary cohomology by the explicit composite $b=\beta_K\circ(e^{-1}\otimes 1_D):Q\otimes^L_\Lambda D\to\Lambda$. Equivalently $b\circ(e\otimes1_D)=\beta_K$. Hence this is exactly the pairing specified in the item, with its original evaluation and normalized trace.

source.place: Step 2, transport of the specified pairing

proof.text: Its adjoint and its canonical inverse. By [thm-pod-derived-poincare-duality], the adjoint $\alpha:D\to C^\vee$ of $\beta_K$ is an isomorphism, with specified canonical inverse $\theta:C^\vee\to D$. All its hypotheses are those of the item: the same coefficient stage, $K\in D^b_{ctf}$, and site-perfectness; that theorem does not require properness. The tensor--internal-Hom adjunction of [sk-def-sf-operations] (i) is natural in its first argument. Consequently the adjoint of the explicit composite in step 3 is $\alpha_b=(e^{-1})^\vee\circ\alpha:D\to Q^\vee$. Here $e^\vee:Q^\vee\to C^\vee$ is precomposition by $e$, and $(e^{-1})^\vee$ is precomposition by $e^{-1}$. These maps are mutually inverse, since precomposition by $e\circ e^{-1}$ or $e^{-1}\circ e$ is precomposition by the identity. Thus $\alpha_b^{-1}=\theta\circ e^\vee:Q^\vee\to D$; the two inverse identities follow by cancelling these pairs and $\alpha\circ\theta$, $\theta\circ\alpha$. This explicitly proves perfectness in [def-pod-perfect-derived-pairing] and identifies the inverse with the canonical duality isomorphism read through the proper comparison. The source perfect point complexes stay perfect under the isomorphism $e$, so the definition has the required domain.

source.place: Step 3, functorial adjoint and canonical inverse

proof.text: The twisted degreewise pairing, only at a field stage. Suppose $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. The theorem [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field] gives finite-dimensional spaces $V_c=H_c^i(X,K)$ and $W_d=H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))$ and says that the adjoint $a_i:W_d\to V_c^\vee$ of the specified degreewise pairing is an isomorphism. The current statement of [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing] applies to the same $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, perfect over $\Lambda_X$, at this selected field stage. It identifies these specific pairings with the degree-zero part of $\beta_K$ using $H^r(C[m])=H^{r+m}(C)$, so $H^{-i}(D)=H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))$. Put $V=H^i(X,K)$. The comparison $e_i:V_c\to V$ of step 2 identifies the degreewise part of $b$ with $b_i(v,w)=\langle e_i^{-1}v,w\rangle_i$. Its adjoint is $a_i'= (e_i^{-1})^\vee\circ a_i:W_d\to V^\vee$, whose inverse is $a_i^{-1}\circ e_i^\vee$. Thus the ordinary-cohomology pairing is perfect and its spaces are finite-dimensional. This argument uses the adjoint of the actual pairing, not just an abstract equality of dimensions.

The line-valued degreewise form. Write $W=H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)$ and $T=\Lambda(d)$. Use the canonical isomorphism expressly stated in the current [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing], $W_d\cong W\otimes_\Lambda T$; its hypotheses hold because the fixed setting has geometric fiber over the algebraically closed $k$. The same statement identifies the line-valued form of this very pairing by eliminating the invertible twist, with values in $T^{-1}=\Lambda(-d)$. This uses the proposition's stated comparison, not a global-sections assertion inferred from the definition of a twist. Concretely its value on $(v,w)$ is the functional $t\mapsto b_i(v,w\otimes t)$ on $T$, regarded as an element of $T^{-1}$. Tensoring the isomorphism $W\otimes T\xrightarrow{a_i'}V^\vee$ from step 5 with $T^{-1}$, and cancelling $T\otimes T^{-1}\cong\Lambda$, gives the isomorphism $W\to V^\vee\otimes T^{-1}$ that is precisely its line-valued adjoint. Equivalently one can transport the perfect compact-support line-valued form asserted in [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field] by the same $e_i$. Therefore the displayed untwisted, line-valued pairing on ordinary cohomology is perfect. No basis or trivialization of the Tate line is chosen.

Statement: the correction from A to Λ is right. def-pod-conventions defines A as the point's coefficient ring, and a literal A_{E,n} target is impossible at the field stages (there is no unital ring map Z/ℓ^n -> Q_ℓ). At Λ=A the statement is unchanged, it matches def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing and thm-pod-derived-poincare-duality, and nothing is weakened; all five citers stay valid. 'Over a field' means the field stages E and Q̄_ℓ, as in the unit, the blueprint proof and the degreewise theorem. Step 1: clause (b) of the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence (Stacks 01W4, morphisms-lemma-base-change-proper) gives properness of a_X after base change, which is enough. Step 2: cor-cbc-proper-coincidence supplies the identity-compactification identification at finite level and prop-weil-proper-compact-coincidence gives it at all stages; applying Fib_s and H^i gives e and e_i. Minor looseness: the prop's statement says only '≅'; its main-20261015 proof shows the map is the levelwise canonical one, and perfectness holds for any isomorphism anyway. Step 3: the elementary definition b=β_K∘(e^{-1}⊗1). Step 4: by naturality in the first variable of the adjunction in sk-def-sf-operations (i), α_b=(e^{-1})^∨∘α with inverse θ∘e^∨; I checked both composites by hand, and Q≅C gives the perfect point-complex domain that def-pod-perfect-derived-pairing requires. Steps 5–6: the degreewise theorem's adjoint isomorphism, the degree-zero identification and the twist isomorphism in prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing, then precomposition by e_i^{-1} and tensoring with T^{-1}; the steps are explicit and choose no trivialization of the Tate line. proof_deps equals the union of the uses, and all steps are under 2000 characters. Route: cor-cbc is Lean-closed, so it is a tool. I accept both declared tool uses: lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence (Mathlib leaf, clause (b) only) and prop-weil-proper-compact-coincidence (all-stage coincidence used as a black box). No SGA is cited. The duplicate search found no other node stating this item. The slopmaster2 Lean is finite-Λ only, and its degreewise result is an abstract isomorphism, so not attaching it is correct. Small cases checked: Spec k, K=0, P^1, shifted K, and A_{E,n} with n≥2 (derived clause only). No fixes.
